reports.title: Reports
reports.funnelHint: How many deals entered each stage and how many moved on to a later one. Deals created mid-funnel make a stage-over-stage comparison misleading, so the rate is progression out of the stage.
reports.forecastHint: Open pipeline by expected month, weighted by probability, against what actually closed in it.
reports.noCloseDate: {{count}} deals with no expected close date ({{value}}) — not in the chart.
reports.velocityHint: Average time in each stage. Only closed intervals count.
reports.lossReasonsHint: The report that changes the sales pitch.
reports.sourcesHint: Where the pipeline comes from, and what each origin actually closes.
reports.revenueHint: Closed value against the hours logged on the tasks that delivered it. Only possible because the CRM lives with the projects.
reports.revenueByServiceHint: What each service sold in won deals. One-time and recurring apart, because mixing a project with a monthly fee hides both.
reports.mrrHint: What comes in every month and where the movement comes from. A pause counts as contraction, not churn: the client did not leave.
reports.acquisitionHint: Clients and revenue per channel, not just deals: a channel with many opportunities and few wins shows up here.
reports.portfolioHint: Who the company works with today. No period: a client base is a state, not a range.
reports.concentrationHint: How much of the recurring revenue sits in the five largest clients.
reports.cohortsHint: Clients grouped by the month they became clients, and how many still had a contract later. Needs a year of history to say anything.
